mechanism_narrative: The current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is always associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as a low rate environment reduces discount rates applied to equity cash flows.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is observed, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.0% signals a tightening monetary policy that increases equity risk premiums, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals an improving economic environment that reduces equity risk premiums, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in FEDFUNDS and UNRATE occurs in more than 40% of instances where the signal is active (i.e., both decline) but SPX produces negative 20-day returns, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS rising > 0.3 percentage points over three months), increased risk aversion and reduced liquidity produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is always associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as a high unemployment rate signals weak economic activity and reduced corporate earnings potential.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE is observed, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level (HOUST) below 1400 thousand units signals a weak housing market, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate central bank stimulus in response to economic weakness.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST < 1400, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) coupled with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate aggressive monetary policy responses.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and INDPRO occurs in more than 40% of instances where the signal is active (i.e., both decline) but SPX produces negative 60-day returns, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock regime (defined by industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 100), increased inflationary pressures and reduced economic growth produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
